newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says it set up new camp for Iraqi refugees.
newsitem.headline: Iran says it set up new camp for Iraqi refugees.

text.p: Iran has set up a new camp on its northwestern border with Iraq to accommodate a continued influx of Kurdish refugees, the official Iranian News Agency IRNA said on Sunday.

IRNA quoted Ali Yari, governor of the northwestern border city of Marivan, as saying the new camp would help cope with an average of 400 refugees who were entering Iran every day through the nearby border crossing at Bashmaq.
He said the construction of the camp would be completed "imminently" and that about 10,000 refugees had already settled in the area.

Iran has so far spent 3 billion rials ($1.7 million at the official exchange rate and $3 million at the black market rate) on foodstuffs, medicine and garments for refugees since they fled recent fighting between rival Kurdish groups in northern Iraq, IRNA quoted Yari as saying.

Iran said last week it was sheltering up to 70,000 Kurdish refugees at several sites on its border with Iraq. The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has said some 40,000 refugees have flooded Iran in recent weeks.
